# pcd_cluster_vmha_config (Resource)

Manages a cluster's VM high-availability settings in hamgr, PCD's VM high-availability service: the evacuation speed and the NFS heartbeat path, which the PCD UI's cluster dialogs also set in PCD releases whose UI has them. Turning VM high availability on or off stays on `pcd_cluster` (`vm_high_availability.enabled`); these settings act while it is on. Set at least one of `evacuation_speed` and `nfs_heartbeat_path`.

hamgr keeps one configuration per cluster and merges every write into it, so this resource takes over whatever the cluster already has: an attribute left out of the configuration keeps the cluster's value and reads it back. hamgr has no way to delete a configuration, so destroying this resource leaves the settings in PCD as they are, removes them from Terraform state, and warns. hamgr keeps them by cluster name, so they also outlive the cluster, and a later cluster of the same name gets them. Writing a configuration needs a cluster that PCD's resource manager knows. hamgr can take up to five minutes to learn of a cluster that was just created, so when hamgr refuses a write for a cluster the resource manager has, the provider retries it for up to six minutes; creating this resource in the same apply as its cluster can therefore wait that long.

Import works for a cluster whose configuration hamgr already holds. For a cluster with none, import fails with "Cannot import non-existent remote object"; declare the resource and apply instead, and the first write creates the configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pcd_cluster" "main" {
  name = "cluster-1"

  vm_high_availability = {
    enabled = true
  }
}

# The cluster's VM high-availability settings: evacuate a failed host's VMs
# with the fastest evacuation speed, and tell a host cut off from the network
# from a failed one through a heartbeat on shared NFS storage, mounted at this
# path on every hypervisor in the cluster.
resource "pcd_cluster_vmha_config" "main" {
  cluster_name       = pcd_cluster.main.name
  evacuation_speed   = "aggressive"
  nfs_heartbeat_path = "/mnt/vmha-heartbeat"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_name` (String) The name of the cluster, for example `pcd_cluster.<name>.name`. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `evacuation_speed` (String) How long PCD waits, once a host stops responding, before it restarts the host's VMs elsewhere: `conservative`, `balanced` or `aggressive` (by the PCD UI's description, about 10, 5 and 2 minutes to the first restart). A shorter wait recovers sooner but is likelier to react to a brief network outage or a routine reboot. A write that carries it, on create and on an update that changes it, also makes hamgr set the cluster's `cooldown` and `host_config.post_delay` to that speed's fixed values (`aggressive` 20 s and 15 s, `balanced` 45 s and 30 s, `conservative` 150 s and 59 s), replacing values set outside this resource, and push `post_delay` to the cluster's hosts that have the VM high-availability role. Omitted, the cluster's value is left as it is and read back; it reads null when the cluster has none, and hamgr then uses its default.
- `nfs_heartbeat_path` (String) A path on shared NFS storage, mounted on every hypervisor in the cluster, where each host writes a liveness heartbeat, so that PCD can tell a host cut off from the network from one that failed: the Storage Heartbeat of the PCD UI's cluster dialogs, in PCD releases whose UI has them. hamgr pushes it to the cluster's hosts that have the VM high-availability role. `""` turns the storage heartbeat off. Omitted, the cluster's value is left as it is and read back (`""` when there is none). Setting it sends hamgr's `host_config` with only this key; this resource does not manage the other host settings hamgr keeps there.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The cluster name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax. The IDs are assigned by PCD; the
[Importing guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/platform9/pcd/latest/docs/guides/importing)
explains how to look them up.

```shell
# The import ID is the cluster name (GET /resmgr/v2/clusters)
terraform import pcd_cluster_vmha_config.main <cluster_name>
```
